claim: The servo-bench identification method recovers a synthetic SCS0009-class servo from a 12 s bench recording (steps then a chirp on a 60 g, 8 cm pendulum, positions quantized to the encoder's 1024 counts over 300 degrees with 2 mrad noise): stall torque 0.255 N*m against 0.25 true, P gain 39.3 duty/rad against 40, back-EMF 0.00408 against 0.004 N*m*s/rad, Coulomb friction 0.0085 against 0.008 N*m, command delay 11.1 against 12 ms, armature 2.8e-5 against 2.0e-5 kg*m^2 (beside the arm's 3.4e-4); held-out position error 5.4 mrad, the noise level. Each estimate is within 2.5 percent of the truth except friction (6 percent), the delay (one integrator step) and the armature (small beside the arm), and the reported 95 percent intervals are narrower than these biases: the encoder's quantization biases one recording systematically, so two or more recordings and their cross-run spread are what earn trust.
instrument: trainnr.robot.servo_bench (numpy semi-implicit Euler at 1 ms, scipy differential evolution then least squares), MuJoCo for the arm's inertia and gravity; RTX 3090 Ti machine, CPU only; 2 min 15 s for the fit with 16 bootstrap replicates

inputs.bench: one hinge (axis y) driving a 10 g capsule and a 50 g sphere at 8 cm; bench.json: servo scs0009, vin 6.0 V, kp 32, max_pwm 1.0
inputs.recording: 50 Hz, 12 s: square steps of +-0.6 rad at 0.5 Hz for 6 s, then a chirp of 0.5 rad from 0.2 Hz rising 0.25 Hz per second; simulated by the method's own law from rest, Gaussian noise 2 mrad, then rounded to 300/1024 degrees

artifacts.robots/scs0009-bench/fits/bench-steps@65: the fit record in the test project
artifacts.robots/scs0009-bench/fits/actuators/scs0: the actuator bundle a legged walk on Microduck Nano's model then trained with (a smoke)

protocol: Synthetic: the truth is simulated by the same law the method fits, so this measures recovery through quantization and noise, not the law's fidelity to a real servo. Blocks of 2 s, each started from its measured position and a fitted starting velocity; the last block held out; intervals the wider of a 16-replicate block bootstrap and the asymptotic interval from the Jacobian, inflated for the residuals' lag-1 autocorrelation.
caveats: Synthetic data: a real SCS0009's law, gearbox and encoder may differ from BAM's first tier; the method's held-out error on a real bench recording is the test of that.
One recording: the intervals are narrower than the quantization's bias on four of six parameters; the cross-run spread over two or more recordings is the honest uncertainty.
Back-EMF and viscous friction are one term from positions; the bundle puts it all in kt^2/R and records friction_viscous 0.
